title: Hasanta, ড, and the n-conjuncts
body:
# Lesson 10: Hasanta, ড, and the n-conjuncts

্ (hasanta) means "no vowel here". Usually you don't see it: two consonants with no vowel between them fuse into one shape, a conjunct (juktakkhor). Here are three with n on top, plus ড (hard d).

| Script | Sound | Note |
|---|---|---|
| ◌্ | hasanta: (no vowel) | A small slash under the letter. Mostly hidden inside conjuncts. |
| ড | do (hard d) | ড় without the dot. Hard d, the pair of ট. |
| ন্ত | nto (nt) | Looks like ন with a ত curl stuck on; read nt. |
| ন্দ | ndo (nd) | ন on the left, দ squeezed on the right. |
| ন্ড | ndo (hard nd) | Older spelling uses ণ্ড: ঠাণ্ডা. Same word. |

## How they combine

ন্ + ত = ন্ত **nt**, ন্ + দ = ন্দ **nd**, ন্ + ড = ন্ড **nd**. Read the conjunct as one cluster: কি + ন্তু = কিন্তু **kintu**.

## Read these

Cover the right side, read the script aloud, then check.

- কিন্তু → kintu: but
- সুন্দর → shundor: beautiful
- ঠান্ডা → thanda: cold
- শান্ত → shanto: calm
- ডাল → dal: lentils (dal)
